problem: Calculate, in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{5}{8}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

feedback.problem: Calculate, in degrees, rounded to $1$ decimal place, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{3}{4}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{3}{4})=48.590\,377{…}^{∘}≈48.590\,{4}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $48.590\,{4}^{∘}$ lies inside the range, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=48.590\,{4}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=48.590\,{4}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=48.590\,{4}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/4864e26ba05324041220dff99d1929b4c280b77456295d00d13d246279b4e628.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}-48.590\,{4}^{∘} \\  & =131.409\,{6}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions (rounded to one decimal place) are $x={48.6}^{∘},{131.4}^{∘}.$
